title: UI events: widget events bound to a destination, lifecycle events, application (system) events, external sites and extended (DOM) events

capabilities.title: Widget and lifecycle events: bind OnClick, OnReady or OnAfterFetch to a destination
capabilities.summary: A built-in widget event (`$btn/OnClick`, `$item/OnClick`, `$link/OnClick`) is born with its widget and is bound with `set <widget>/OnClick Destination <target>`, where the target is a screen action (`$action`, `IScreenAction:<Name>`), a screen (`IMobileScreen:<Name>`, navigation) or an external site; navigation arguments are `set <widget>/OnClick/<Parameter> Value <expr>`. Lifecycle events (`$scr/OnReady`, `$da/OnAfterFetch`) are bound the same way. This capability owns the binding only; the body of the target is declared by the logic capabilities.

route.operation: set {target: '<widget>/OnClick' | '<screen>/OnReady' | '<dataAction>/OnAfterFetch', prop: 'Destination', value: '<screen action | IMobileScreen:Name | external site>'}; set {target: '<widget>/OnClick/<Input>', prop: 'Value', value: '<expr>'}

capabilities.guidance: The chain is widget -> event -> action -> data: create the widget (ui.widget, ui.input, ui.list), create or reuse the screen action (logic), then bind the event Destination; a Destination must name an element that already exists at that op of the job. Built-in events navigate or call logic with a Destination; a block instance event uses a Handler (ui.block-instance); an extended DOM event (IEvent) uses a Handler (logic.app-event). A screen action bound to an event must have no outputs. An event of a block instance in the html fragment: @Event="ScreenAction" on <Block name="B">, with :Input="expr" for its inputs and <slot name="P"> for its placeholders.

limits.text: Two event families on the same widget: the built-in event (IBuiltinEvent, OnClick) navigates or calls logic through Destination; an extended event (IEvent) calls a screen action through Handler. usages of an external site names the IBuiltinEvent OnClick, not the IEvent.

Screen and block lifecycle events (OnInitialize, OnReady, OnDestroy, OnParametersChanged) and a Data Action OnAfterFetch are bound with Destination like any built-in event; OnRender is in the vocabulary but not exercised by a job.

differences: the OnClick object is recorded as IBuiltinEvent

limits.text: A navigation Destination must name a screen created earlier in the job: the preflight refuses forward references and names the op numbers.
Traditional Web screens run their data fetch in the Preparation (not a lifecycle event); that is a logic element (A) of ui.traditional-screen.
Screen and block lifecycle events (OnInitialize, OnReady, OnDestroy, OnParametersChanged) are bound with Destination; OnRender and a Data Action OnAfterFetch are not exercised by an O11 suite job.

differences: the OnClick object's interface is OutSystems.Model.UI.Mobile.Events.IUILifeCycleEvent (ledger of the stamped O11 results), so the widget-event and lifecycle-event roles share one native type on O11

recommends.when: the Destination is a screen action: its body, inputs and assignments are declared there
the lifecycle event is the OnAfterFetch of a Data Action

capabilities.title: Application events, external sites and extended (DOM) events
capabilities.summary: ISystemEvent (OnApplicationReady; one fixed place per app, the flow is born empty), IExternalSite (a UI flow node with an URL, the destination of a widget event that leaves the app) and IEvent (an extended DOM event of a widget, handled by a screen action without outputs).

route.operation: create ISystemEvent at @espace | IExternalSite in IMobileFlow:<Flow> | IEvent under a widget; set Event/Handler/URL; the system event body is a logic flow edited by path

capabilities.guidance: The name given to `create ISystemEvent` is ignored: the factory order of this build yields OnApplicationReady; read @espace back to see which one was born, then author its Start/body/End. An extended event has no name of its own: it is named after its Event (closed list of 11 DOM names).

create.route: create {parent: @espace, type: ISystemEvent} | {parent: IMobileFlow:<Flow>, type: IExternalSite, name} | {parent: <widget>, type: IEvent}
preconditions: ISystemEvent: the four factories take no argument, the name is ignored and one fixed place per app is filled (this build: OnApplicationReady); the flow is born empty (Start is required)
IExternalSite: the parent is the UI flow, never a screen; an input parameter named URL makes the URL dynamic
IEvent: any top-level widget can carry extended events (IContainer.CreateEvent())

odc.scope: OnApplicationReady born empty, then Start/assign/End authored and read back

o11.scope: cat-b-app-events: create (op 3) answered by IESpace.CreateOnApplicationReady (the first ISystemEvent factory by reflection order; get @espace, op 16); Start, Assign and End authored in it (ops 5-14)

odc.scope: two external sites in MainFlow, one with an URL input parameter
on a container and on an input; born without name, Event and Handler

preconditions: IEvent.Event is a closed list of 11 DOM event names; Handler accepts a screen action without outputs

key <espace>.#OnApplicationReady; Nodes and IsValid before and after editing

Event and Handler of a born and of an inherited extended event
the consumer is the button's IBuiltinEvent OnClick

o11.alternative: the name is the fixed place of the event (OnApplicationReady)

odc.scope: inherited external site renamed; the button OnClick keeps the same Destination by key

odc.note: the platform refuses rename on IEvent (job:platform-events-lifecycle description; kernel/docs/NAO-DA.md; no negative job)
odc.alternative: set Event: the name is derived from the DOM event

No O11 suite job exercises ISystemEvent, IExternalSite or IEvent: every operation is undetermined on O11 (the verbs are the shared kernel's; the behaviour is not measured).
